subject: Model runbook readiness checklist & latency percentiles
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam@orchidai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@orchidai.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — model fit ask

Thanks again for the call this morning, Vivek. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope a pilot: 

- Workload: customer support summarization + structured extraction for billing questions. Typical request ~220 tokens (post-system), 95th ~520 tokens.
- Target steady TPS: ~120 TPS, peak bursts up to 400 TPS.
- Quality SLOs: human acceptance >= 92% on the summary task; hallucination rate < 2% on extraction fields.
- Latency target (user-facing): p95 <= 150ms, p99 ideally <= 300ms for seq_len=128 payloads; for longer flows (seq_len=512) p95 up to 350ms acceptable but p99 ideally < 700ms.

Can you share Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS, p50/p95/p99) for recommended model variants at sequence lengths 128 and 512? Also we'd like a prompt pack (seed prompts + guardrails) and a short note on how Redwood surfaces quality regressions (what signals you alert on). Procurement is on a 6-week timeline — would like a recommended pilot plan that fits that window.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Carter
Head of Product Engineering, OrchidAI
---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam@orchidai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — model fit ask

Appreciate the clear summary, Sam — this is very helpful. Below is a concise post-call recap + recommended next steps and links to Redwood-verified perf profiles.

1) Recommended model slate (initial):
   - redwood-rw-3b-quant (low-cost/high-throughput) — good for high TPS routing and prefix caching.
   - redwood-7b-ptq (balanced quality/latency) — recommended for initial pilot to hit quality SLOs.
   - redwood-chat-7b-ops (chat-optimized variant) — if you want to enable tool-calling/structured extraction in a single model.

2) Redwood-verified performance (summary, internal benchmark lab, seq_len=128 / seq_len=512):
   - redwood-rw-3b-quant: seq128 -> sustained 340 TPS (single-GPU pool), p50 36ms, p95 110ms, p99 230ms. seq512 -> sustained 90 TPS, p50 180ms, p95 420ms, p99 760ms.
   - redwood-7b-ptq: seq128 -> sustained 210 TPS, p50 48ms, p95 140ms, p99 300ms. seq512 -> sustained 58 TPS, p50 220ms, p95 480ms, p99 860ms.
   - redwood-chat-7b-ops: seq128 -> sustained 160 TPS, p50 55ms, p95 160ms, p99 340ms. seq512 -> sustained 45 TPS, p50 260ms, p95 520ms, p99 980ms.

(Full result matrices and test artifacts attached / linked below.)

3) Notes on SLA and hosting modes:
   - Hosted (Redwood API): numbers above are from our hosted perf pool under realistic arrival patterns with continuous batching and KV caching turned on. For p99 guarantees we recommend the Dedicated SKU (reserved capacity) if you need contractual latency bounds under peak bursts.
   - Dedicated: with a reserved 4-GPU pool we expect ~+30% headroom on sustained TPS and ~15-25% improvement on p99 for seq128.

4) Quality/regression guardrails (high level):
   - We run nightly evals against your holdout prompt set and track: acceptance rate, hallucination rate (field-level mismatch), and semantic similarity drift.
   - We wire alerts on: >2% drop in acceptance over a rolling 24h window, >1% uptick in hallucination rate, and any sudden latency spikes beyond configured SLO.
   - See attached runbook for integrating our eval webhooks and auto-fallbacks.

Attachments: runbook_v1.pdf (pilot runbook, QA checklist), latency_heatmap_seq128_512.png (visual p99 snapshots)
Links: https://redwood.ai/perf-profiles/rw-3b-quant (profile), https://redwood.ai/evals/ORCH-2028-04/bench-20280714 (bench dashboard)

Next steps (proposed):
  - We’ll share a prompt pack and a small guarded eval harness for you to run on a dev subset (attached by Laura).
  - If you’re good, propose a 4-week pilot: week 1 integration + smoke tests, week 2 quality tuning, week 3 load run, week 4 production rollout plan + run-rate pricing.
  - I can schedule a 30-min technical kickoff Tuesday or Wednesday next week — which works for you?

Marking Priya from your side and happy to sync — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam@orchidai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Prompt pack + eval harness (attached)

Forwarding the prompt pack we discussed. Attachment contains: seed prompts, negative examples, guardrail templates, and an eval harness that runs acceptance/hallucination checks against a labeled set. A few integration notes here: 

- prompt_pack_v3.jsonl: single-line JSONL with fields (id, system_prompt, user_prompt, expected_structured_output). Use the "eval_harness.sh" (in repo) to run a quick local pass — it will generate per-example similarity and a hallucination flag.
- Suggested thresholds (pilot): acceptance >= 92%, hallucination_rate <= 2.0%, avg token-generation latency p95 <= 150ms (seq128).
- Regression gating: we recommend a canary rollout on 10% traffic with automatic rollback if acceptance drops >2% vs baseline on the holdout set.

Attachment: prompt_pack_v3.jsonl (see attachments list)

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Carter <sam@orchidai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 15:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model runbook readiness checklist & latency percentiles

Thanks Vivek / Laura — this is exactly what we needed. Couple quick clarifications before we lock the pilot: 

- Can you paste the raw p99 numbers for seq=512 under a sustained concurrency of 50 on Hosted? The table above is helpful but the procurement team specifically asks for the validated p99 when concurrency=50.
- If we go Dedicated, how many GPUs would you recommend to keep p99(seq512) consistently < 700ms at our peak burst (400 TPS)?
- We want the mutual action plan in HubSpot for procurement cadence — can you link that up and include the standard kickoff PO checklist?

Also — would prefer a Tues 10:00 AM PT kickoff.

Sam
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam@orchidai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model runbook readiness checklist & latency percentiles

Great questions — answers below with links to the underlying test artifacts.

1) Raw p99 numbers (Hosted, measured in our lab with concurrency=50, seq_len=512, arrival pattern matching your burst profile):
   - redwood-rw-3b-quant: p99 = 760ms (see testrun ID: bench-ORCH-20280714-RW3B-conc50) -> https://redwood.ai/evals/ORCH-2028-04/bench-20280714#run=bench-ORCH-20280714-RW3B-conc50
   - redwood-7b-ptq: p99 = 860ms (run ID: bench-ORCH-20280714-7BPTQ-conc50) -> https://redwood.ai/evals/ORCH-2028-04/bench-20280714#run=bench-ORCH-20280714-7BPTQ-conc50
   - redwood-chat-7b-ops: p99 = 980ms (run ID: bench-ORCH-20280714-CHAT7B-conc50) -> https://redwood.ai/evals/ORCH-2028-04/bench-20280714#run=bench-ORCH-20280714-CHAT7B-conc50

2) Dedicated guidance (to keep p99(seq512) consistently < 700ms at 400 TPS bursts):
   - We recommend a reserved 6xA100 equivalent GPU pool with autoscaling headroom to 8 GPUs during peak bursts. With that footprint using our optimized kernels and continuous batching you should see p99 drop ~25-35% vs Hosted measured numbers — that aligns with p99(seq512) in the ~480-650ms band depending on model. We can provide an exact Dedicated sizing quote after a brief load-run (we include that in the pilot).

3) HubSpot & procurement artifacts:
   - Mutual action plan + PO kickoff checklist: https://hubspot.com/deal/ORCH-2028-04/mutual-action-plan (I added the standard kickoff PO checklist to the doc).

4) Next immediate steps and meeting:
   - I scheduled the 30-min technical kickoff for Tue 2028-07-18 10:00 AM PT (invitation sent).
   - Action items: Redwood -> provision test tokens + runbook + attach eval harness (we've attached runbook_v1.pdf and prompt_pack_v3.jsonl). OrchidAI -> run the harness on a dev subset and share the first-run metrics by EOD next Thursday.

5) Risk & mitigation summary (short):
   - Risk: p99 spikes on long sequences during sustained bursts -> Mitigation: Dedicated reserved capacity + prefix caching + adaptive batching; automatic model fallback to rw-3b-quant for non-critical paths.
   - Risk: quality regressions post-quantization -> Mitigation: nightly label-based regression checks + canary rollout with 10% traffic and auto-rollback rules.

Attachments referenced: runbook_v1.pdf, latency_heatmap_seq128_512.png, prompt_pack_v3.jsonl
Links: https://redwood.ai/perf-profiles/rw-3b-quant, https://redwood.ai/evals/ORCH-2028-04/bench-20280714, https://hubspot.com/deal/ORCH-2028-04/mutual-action-plan

See you Tue 10:00 — Vivek
